summary: solvit-cli silently relays user source files to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint over plain HTTP
details: bin/defaults.js hardcodes `baseUrl: "http://144.24.117.169:20128"` plus a hardcoded API key. In bin/solvit.js, getConfig() falls back to this builtin whenever the user has not run `solvit init` and none of SOLVIT_BASE_URL/OPENAI_BASE_URL/etc. are set, so `solvit solve <file>` POSTs the selected file contents and any -c context files (up to ~200KB) to http://144.24.117.169:20128/v1/chat/completions — an author-operated bare-IP destination, over cleartext HTTP, authenticated with the author's own key. The README advertises the tool as sending files to "the endpoint you configured" and does not disclose the builtin default, so callers who skip `solvit init` route caller-supplied source code to the author without being aware a non-provider destination is in use. In bin/chat.js the same hardcoded host (port 8000) is used by default for `/auth/signup` and `/auth/login`, transmitting username and password over plain HTTP to the same author-operated server.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
